sources.title: Order of 31 July 2026: Brazilian ordinary-passport exemption for French Guiana
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual JORF publication, NOR INTV2619705A, JORF 178 of 1 August 2026, text 6. All three articles and the entry-into-force notice were read. Article 1 expressly derogates from the 2011 Annex II; Article 2 specifies six months from 31 July 2026.

policies.title: Brazilian ordinary passports: temporary French Guiana visitor waiver
policies.summary: A July 2026 autonomous order grants Brazilian ordinary-passport holders visa-free French Guiana short visits for up to 30 days in any 180-day period. The prefecture identifies the six-month trial as running from 31 July 2026 until 31 January 2027, subject to ordinary admission requirements and excluding commercial activity.
conditions: Scope is Brazilian ordinary passports for non-commercial short visitor travel to French Guiana only. It is not permission to work, reside, study or conduct commercial activity, and does not establish entry to another French territory.

Article 2 literally provides six months from 31 July 2026. The prefecture expressly states until 31 January 2027; that named endpoint supplies the inclusive effectiveTo, not a conversion of months into days. Renewal is possible but not established or assumed.

The initial order's notice and operative Article 2 name 31 July 2026, while the consolidated site's article-version metadata starts on 2 August 2026 after JORF publication on 1 August. The candidate preserves the expressly stated operational start; this metadata distinction is not concealed.

The prefecture requires a passport valid at least three months after the intended return to Brazil, issued less than ten years ago and containing at least two blank pages. It also requires medical-insurance evidence covering the whole stay for at least EUR 30,000, financial guarantees according to accommodation, and yellow-fever vaccination evidence.
Land entrants from Brazil and river arrivals at Saint-Georges must report to the border-police checkpoint at the international bridge. The waiver does not guarantee admission or remove border checks.

The new ordinary-passport waiver does not impose a biometric-passport, Amapá-residence, organised-tour, frontier-card or third-country-visa prerequisite. The old Annex II's narrower exceptions are not conditions of this temporary general visitor waiver.

For historical reconciliation, Annex II separately describes registered-agency trips shorter than fifteen days, specified air stopovers no longer than three days with onward tickets, a local 72-hour frontier-card route for eligible Oiapoque residents, and emergency-team missions. These special routes do not justify a permanent nationality-wide exemption or an automatic post-trial prior-visa conclusion.

France-Visas separately describes qualifying residence-permit and long-stay-visa exemptions; a generic Schengen short-stay visa is not itself permission to enter an overseas territory. Those document-based routes are not prerequisites for this Brazilian trial waiver. Recheck the operative regime before the trial ends; no successor or post-expiry status is asserted.

allowedStays.label: Up to 30 days in any 180-day period
notes: Article 1's visitor-stay limit is distinct from the six-month duration of the temporary policy and from passport validity.
The Act and the prefecture's opening paragraph say not exceeding 30 days. Later shorthand on the prefecture page says less than 30; the explicit statutory inclusive limit controls.

conflicts.explanation: The bundled fallback and the existing broad French Guiana prior-visa policy retain the underlying Annex II treatment. The autonomous order of 31 July 2026 expressly derogates from that annex for Brazilian ordinary-passport short visitors during a six-month trial, with 30 days in 180 and a prefecture-stated endpoint of 31 January 2027. This conflict uses the bundled fallback required by the validator. The separately reported live visa_free/unverified observation agrees with the current temporary category but is not evidence or a permanent waiver.
